open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input representation
open_points.text: “Inputs: One JSON value.” does not preserve the original numeric token required by “an integer spelling that an IEEE double neither holds exactly nor writes as its shortest round-trip form (`18014398509481991`) is refused”
open_points.question: What representation must canonical_bytes receive so it can distinguish the newly refused integer spelling from other spellings that decode to the same runtime number?
options: Receive the original JSON text or token stream and parse it itself
Receive a parsed value plus every original number lexeme
Have each caller perform the spelling check before passing a parsed value
open_points.default_guess: Receive the original JSON text and perform the numeric-spelling check while parsing it.

open_points.subject: json_depth_max during content identity computation
open_points.text: A01 says a value “nested deeper than `json_depth_max` ... is refused where it enters”, while A20 says request-carried JSON texts are “measured on [their] own, so the message around [them] adds nothing” and “A record the store holds entered that way, so its values and schemas are never measured again”; content_identity nevertheless canonicalises an assembled record whose wrappers can make an accepted schema or value deeper than the limit.
open_points.question: When canonical_bytes or content_identity canonicalises internally assembled meaning facts, is json_depth_max applied to the whole assembled document, only to the individual JSON texts at their original entry boundaries, or not at all at that call?
options: Apply depth only at each external entry boundary and never to later wrappers
Apply depth to every complete value passed to canonical_bytes or content_identity
Pass entry-boundary metadata so canonical_values knows which subtexts must be measured
open_points.default_guess: Apply depth only to each external JSON text at entry and do not remeasure it merely because identity wrappers add nesting.

open_points.subject: run_values.assemble_mapped_lists and run_graph.plan_run
open_points.text: assemble_mapped_lists outputs only “or that one list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`”, and plan_run enforces only “a mapped list over `stored_value_bytes_max` failing its node with no record”, while A13 now also requires failure for a list “which nests deeper than `json_depth_max`”.
open_points.question: What result must assemble_mapped_lists return for an over-depth mapped list, and how must plan_run distinguish or consume that result to fail the mapped node and derive the trace?
options: Return one generic mapped-list-limit failure for either byte size or depth
Return distinct over-size and over-depth results with the same node consequence
Have plan_run measure depth independently after assemble_mapped_lists returns the list
open_points.default_guess: Return distinct over-size and over-depth results from assemble_mapped_lists, with plan_run giving both the same recordless mapped-node failure consequence.
